hypotheses.name: Reactivation tuberculosis with cavitary lesion
hypotheses.basis: History of prior TB + haemoptysis + upper lobe cavitary lesion with fibrotic changes and volume loss is classic for reactivation TB; cavities in TB are typically thin-walled and upper lobe predominant

hypotheses.name: Aspergilloma in pre-existing TB cavity
hypotheses.basis: Air crescent sign (if present) could suggest fungus ball within a chronic cavity; however, the image shows no clear dense ball within cavity—only lucency and surrounding fibrosis

hypotheses.name: Squamous cell carcinoma with cavitation
hypotheses.basis: Cavitated lung cancer can mimic TB cavity, especially in smokers; but lacks typical fibrotic halo and is more irregular/wall-thickened; not clearly seen here
